title: Shadow Copy
pitch: Film a job once; it becomes an illustrated SOP, a trainee quiz, and a live watcher that catches missed steps
problem: In every trade and factory, the real procedure lives in one expert's hands. When they retire, quit or take leave, quality walks out with them — new hires relearn by breaking things, and nobody can prove a job was done right.
how: Phone records the expert doing the job once. Spark 1.3 (video) segments the take into steps; Voice Transcribe lifts the narration; SAM 3.1 segments tools/parts per step; Muse Image renders clean step cards; Spark writes the checkpoint list and trainee quiz. Live mode: a tripod phone + SAM 3.1 (Glimmer at the edge) ticks off steps in real time and flags skips before sign-off.
demo: Film the presenter making pour-over coffee. 60 seconds later the SOP appears with step cards. Then the presenter does it WRONG (skips the rinse); the live watcher flags the skipped step with a red overlay before the cup is done.

title: Manual Oracle
pitch: Photograph any machine plate to get the exact manual page, spoken in the worker's language, in seconds
problem: A 1990s lathe or chiller stops at 2am. The manual is a 400-page PDF in German or English; the night technician speaks Bengali. Downtime is a phone-tree of guesses.
how: Pre-load manuals (1M-context Spark ingests entire PDF sets per machine class). Technician photographs the nameplate; Spark matches model, retrieves the exact section, and Voice Transcribe speaks the procedure back in the worker's language with diagrams highlighted.
demo: Point at the machine plate; the exact page renders with the fault procedure spoken aloud in Bengali — while a competitor app is still 'uploading your PDF'.

title: Claim-Ready
pitch: Damage photos plus a 3-minute dictation become an adjuster-grade claim packet that survives scrutiny
problem: Small insurers and field-service firms lose claims on paperwork, not facts: photos unordered, no timestamps, narrative inconsistent with evidence. Adjusters bounce the file; payment takes weeks.
how: Field tech photographs damage (SAM 3.1 crops each damaged part), dictates what happened; Spark 1.3 cross-checks the narrative against every photo (dates, consistency, missing shots), orders the evidence, and renders a claim packet PDF with exhibit numbers.
demo: Live: 6 messy photos + rambling voice note in, one numbered claim packet out — with the app flagging 'no wide shot of the roof; add one' before submission.

title: Defect Atlas
pitch: Every QC photo from every line lands on one defect map with root-cause clusters nobody can deny
problem: QC photos pile up on line supervisors' phones. The same stitch defect recurs for three weeks before anyone connects it to the new fabric batch — by then, 4,000 units are affected.
how: QC photos flow into one store; SAM 3.1 segments and classifies the defect region; Spark clusters by type, line, shift, material batch; the Atlas renders a live defect map with root-cause hypotheses and which batch/shift correlates.
demo: Import 200 sample QC photos; the Atlas instantly shows stitch-defect cluster pinned to one batch and one shift — the meeting argument ends in 10 seconds.

title: Tripwire
pitch: Hours of worksite footage collapse into the twenty seconds that matter, with near-misses auto-flagged
problem: After an incident, investigators scroll 9 hours of footage. Near-misses never get analyzed at all — so the same ladder, the same blind corner, keeps producing accidents. Consent-first: crew badges out, footage auto-deleted in 72h.
how: Phone or cheap camera records the work area (crew-consented). SAM 3.1 tracks zones/persons/objects; Spark reviews only flagged windows (person in fall zone, missing harness at height, vehicle-pedestrian close approach) and renders a near-miss digest.
demo: Play 3 hours of workshop footage; Tripwire surfaces 4 near-miss clips with zone overlays and a one-page digest — the 'how did you find that so fast' moment.

title: Shift Echo
pitch: The end-of-shift voice log becomes the next crew's one-page briefing — nothing falls between shifts
problem: Between the day and night shift, everything falls: which machine is acting up, which order is urgent, which valve sticks. Handover is a sticky note, so night shift rediscovers day shift's problems.
how: Outgoing lead talks for 90 seconds (Voice Transcribe with diarization); Spark structures it into machine status, open orders, hazards, and carry-overs; the incoming crew gets a one-page briefing card plus a WhatsApp digest.
demo: Record a rambling 90-second handover; Echo prints the one-page briefing instantly and answers 'what's the first thing to check tonight?' out loud.

title: Quote Engine
pitch: Photos of the job plus a 2-minute dictation become an itemized priced estimate before you leave the driveway
problem: Trades lose jobs to whoever quotes first. Pricing lives in the owner's head — square meters, materials, labor hours — so quotes go out 3 days late or not at all.
how: Tech photographs the site; Spark 1.3 measures/detects scope (SAM-assisted area estimates from a reference card), combines with the spoken specifics and a price book; the itemized PDF estimate lands in the client's WhatsApp before the van door closes.
demo: Walk the room filming 4 walls; 90 seconds later a priced, itemized estimate PDF exists — item lines tap-editable live.

title: Kit Check
pitch: One photo of any safety kit flags missing items against its own checklist — in 5 seconds
problem: Fire extinguishers expire, first-aid kits lose items, emergency kits get raided — and the failure is discovered the day it's needed. Compliance checks are annual; reality is daily.
how: Define kit checklists once (extinguisher, first-aid, spill kit, tool kit). A photo; SAM 3.1 segments present items, Spark matches against the checklist and flags missing/expired/misplaced with a printable QR compliance card.
demo: Photograph a med kit with the bandage box secretly removed — red flag in 5 seconds with the exact missing item circled.

title: Planogram Eye
pitch: Store staff photograph shelves; HQ sees planogram compliance, gaps and expiry across all branches
problem: Minimart chains fly blind between branch visits: gaps, misplaced products, expired stock, competitor facings. Planogram compliance is checked by area managers driving around once a month.
how: Each morning a staffer films the aisle once; SAM 3.1 segments facings and detects gaps/expired labels; Spark compares to the planogram and renders HQ's branch heatmap with a restock list per store.
demo: Film a bookshelf-as-shelf with a planted gap and an 'expired' tag; the heatmap flags both with locations — instantly, from one phone video.

title: Agent Files
domain: back offices stuck on legacy software
pitch: Muse Wonder operates the 20-year-old desktop app: photos in, records filed, no API needed
problem: Distributors, clinics and land offices run on legacy desktop software with no API. Data entry clerks retype documents all day; the queue grows every month.
how: Scan/photo documents; Spark extracts fields; Wonder's computer-use operates the legacy UI (menus, tabs, dialogs) exactly like a temp worker — filing records, handling error dialogs, and reporting what it filed with screenshots.
demo: Screen-share: 5 scanned invoices get typed into a mock legacy ERP by the agent, complete with a wrong-tab recovery — while the coffee is still hot.

title: Season Oracle
pitch: Dump the entire year's messy records into one chat; get the owner's briefing you never had time to write
problem: Owners survive the season but never analyze it: which product line bled money, which week over-ordered, which crew was fastest. The data exists — in 40 spreadsheets, notebooks and chats nobody has time to read.
how: Point Spark 1.3's 1M context at the whole year: ledgers, photos, voice notes, WhatsApp exports. It returns the season briefing: top losses, hidden wins, next-season plan with numbers — every claim citing the source row.
demo: Drop 12 months of deliberately messy files; Oracle answers 'what should I cut next season?' in 20 seconds with three cited receipts.

title: Warranty Wrapper
pitch: Repair photos auto-bundle into warranty-proof packs that get claims approved the first time
problem: Warranty claims die on missing evidence: no before photos, no serial capture, no timestamp proof. Shops eat the cost; customers blame the shop.
how: Every repair flows through a guided capture (serial, before, part, after); Spark assembles the evidence pack with timestamps and a claim letter; one tap submits or stores for later claims.
demo: Show a rejected claim (missing evidence), then the Wrapper pack: serial photo, defect close-up, part swap — approved letter drafted, ready to send.

title: Machine Notebook
pitch: The pile of service notebooks becomes searchable equipment history cards — 'what did we do last time?' answered
problem: Every workshop has the notebook: 'Mar 12: replaced bearing, vibrates when cold.' It's unsearchable, at the mercy of handwriting and memory. The same fault gets re-diagnosed twice a year.
how: Photograph notebook pages and service tags; Spark transcribes/structures into per-machine history cards (date, fault, part, fix, cost); search by symptom — 'vibrates when cold' returns the card plus the exact photo.
demo: Import 10 photographed pages; ask 'when did the compressor last act up?' — the card, photo and fix appear; a paper pile would still be in a drawer.

title: Site Diary
pitch: Site photos and a 2-minute voice note become the daily log, progress percent and early warnings
problem: Site engineers write daily logs from memory at 9pm, or never. Disputes over 'what was done by when' cost months; delays are visible only after they're expensive.
how: Each evening the engineer films a walkthrough and talks; Spark structures the diary entry, SAM 3.1 verifies staged work against the plan (rebar placed, slab poured), progress percent updates, and deviations trigger early-warning flags.
demo: Two weeks of simulated site photos replay into a progress curve with one red-flagged 'column curing skipped' warning — the dispute-settling moment.

title: Stitch Card
pitch: Customer photos become perfect-fit measurement cards — fewer refits, happier brides, faster tailors
problem: Tailoring refits are the #1 cost: measurements misread, transcribed wrong, or guessed. Each refit costs a day and goodwill; wedding-season piles make it worse.
how: Guided photo set (front/side with a reference card); SAM 3.1 extracts landmarks; Spark converts to the shop's measurement card format with confidence flags, and prints the production card with cut notes.
demo: Photograph a dressed mannequin; the card prints with measurements within tolerance — plus a flag where the photo is ambiguous ('arm not relaxed').

title: Cold Chain Verdict
pitch: Photograph the temperature gauge; get a violation log and a product-safety verdict auditors accept
problem: Cold stores log temps on paper twice a day; night deviations go unnoticed, and when a batch spoils nobody can prove when it was safe. Insurers and buyers want records that don't exist.
how: Any phone photographs analog gauges/digital displays each shift; Spark reads the dial, logs against thresholds, and maintains a violation timeline; a batch-level verdict ('safe / watch / discard') attaches to every SKU with evidence photos.
demo: Point at a gauge photo set simulating a night failure: the timeline shows the 3-hour excursion and the exact batches affected — proof, not memory.

title: Harvest Ledger
pitch: Members' field voice notes become the co-op ledger — weights, grades and payments in one place
problem: Co-op clerks chase paper slips from 200 farmers; payments lag, disputes fester, and the co-op can't prove quantities to buyers. The ledger is always a week behind reality.
how: At the weighbridge, the clerk (or farmer) speaks: name, crop, weight, grade; Voice Transcribe + Spark structure the entry with a photo of the scale; the ledger, per-member statements and buyer reports build themselves — Bengali voice-first.
demo: Speak 6 rapid entries in Bengali; the ledger updates live and prints a member statement — while the paper system is still finding a pen.

title: Fleet Whisper
pitch: Drivers film a 60-second walkaround; the fleet's vehicle check log writes itself and defects get routed
problem: Daily vehicle checks are ticked without walking around. When a tire blows, there's no record the crack existed — liability lands on the owner, and defect repairs start days late.
how: Driver films the walkaround while talking; Spark matches narration to visible defects (crack, wear, leak), files the check log, routes the defect to the mechanic with the clip attached, and flags repeat offenders.
demo: Walk around a car pointing out a real scuff + a 'hidden' defect: the log appears with the defect timecoded, routed to 'mechanic' — the unticked-box era ends.

title: Borrow Book
pitch: Photograph the tool tag; the store knows who has what, since when, and what's overdue
problem: 'Who took the torque wrench?' eats an hour a day. Tools migrate between crews and vanish; replacements are bought in a panic. The whiteboard borrow-list is always stale.
how: Issue = photo of the worker's badge + tool tag; return = photo again. Spark reads tags and maintains the custody board; overdue items ping the owner; monthly: the top-loss report.
demo: Photograph 3 checkouts rapid-fire; then ask 'where is the impact driver?' — the answer with photo, person and due date, before the whiteboard would even be found.

title: Job Cost Ghost
pitch: Job photos plus receipts become a true profitability card per job — before the invoice, not after
problem: Contractors price jobs by gut and discover the truth at invoice time: material overruns invisible, rework uncounted. Some 'busy' jobs are quietly losing money for months.
how: Snap receipts and site photos against the job; Spark extracts costs, flags scope creep vs the estimate (photos show extra work), and maintains a live profitability card with a 'quote vs reality' delta.
demo: Feed one job's mess (9 receipts, 6 photos); the card shows the job is 12% underwater with the exact overrun line and photo — the gut-check becomes a number.

title: Dispatch Untangler
pitch: Drivers talk, dispatchers finally trust the board: voice updates become a live dispatch map
problem: Drivers call dispatch with 'stuck near the bridge, unloading 20 minutes'; the whiteboard and three WhatsApp groups diverge; customers hear a different story each time.
how: Driver voice updates (any language) become structured board events (location, delay, POD); Spark resolves conflicts between calls and the plan; the dispatcher sees one live board with exceptions highlighted, customers get honest ETAs.
demo: Three overlapping rambling calls play; the board self-updates with one exception flagged — 'truck 7 will miss the 4pm window; reassign stop 12' proposed in one tap.

title: Line Clearance
pitch: A photo proves the line is clear before restart — changeover errors caught before they become recalls
problem: Changeover mistakes (previous batch's label, leftover allergen ingredient) are the root of the worst recalls. Paper checklists are signed in haste; evidence doesn't exist.
how: Operator photographs the line per checklist zone; SAM 3.1 verifies absence/presence (stray packaging, wrong label roll, tools left behind); Spark generates the clearance certificate with evidence, timestamped and signable.
demo: Planted leftover label roll on the mock line: red flag with the item circled; cleared version prints the certificate — the auditor's favorite 20 seconds.

title: Print Doctor
pitch: A camera pass over proofs catches prepress errors before the ink — reprints become rare
problem: Print shops reprint 5-10% of runs for errors a second pair of eyes would catch: low-res images, missing bleed, wrong phone number, CMYK disasters. Reruns erase the margin.
how: Photograph the proof + load the source file; Spark compares (text diff against customer order, resolution/bleed checks, color warnings) and prints a go/no-go card with the exact fixes.
demo: A proof with a swapped digit in the phone number: red circle + 'order said 1717, proof says 1177' — the rerun that never happens.

title: Waste Watch
pitch: One photo of the bin line a day reveals the money being thrown away — and the fix
problem: Waste is the invisible line item: over-prepped batter, expired stock, offcuts. Staff know it; owners never see it aggregated. 'Reduce waste' dies without evidence.
how: End-of-day bin photo (top-down); Spark identifies and estimates quantity/value of wasted categories; the weekly waste report shows the top 3 money-binned items with trend and one concrete fix each.
demo: Seven days of bin photos replay into a bar chart: 'batter = 4,200 tk/week over-prep; cut batch size after 7pm' — the owner visibly recalculates.

title: Grading Scale
pitch: Produce photos get an instant grade and fair price band — farmers stop guessing, buyers stop haggling
problem: Price discovery at the farm gate is a negotiation against information asymmetry: the trader knows the grade; the farmer guesses. Everyone loses time; the co-op loses margin.
how: Photo of the sample crate; Spark grades against published grade sheets (size, color, defect count via segmentation) and returns the grade + today's fair price band with citations; the co-op ledger logs the deal.
demo: Grade the same crate twice (with and without blemish zoom) — different grades, different bands, instant. The farmer's phone becomes the price reference.

title: Trainee Sim
pitch: The SOP becomes an interactive trainee quiz with generated 'spot the mistake' scenes — training that sticks
problem: Training is a video nobody finishes or a shadowing week nobody remembers. Trainees touch real machines before they're ready because there's no safe middle ground.
how: From the filmed SOP (or text procedure), Spark generates scenario questions; Muse Image renders realistic 'spot the mistake' scenes of the actual workplace; trainees tap through on a shared phone; supervisors see readiness scores.
demo: Play one generated scene: the PPE missing at step 3 of YOUR actual procedure; trainee taps the error; the readiness score ticks up — training by simulation, not lecture.

title: Intake Triage
pitch: The walk-in explains by voice; the case opens, routes and books itself — the queue moves itself
problem: Front desks are the bottleneck: one receptionist, four queues, a ringing phone. Intake forms are half-empty; urgent cases wait behind paperwork.
how: The visitor speaks to the desk mic; Voice Transcribe + Spark fill the intake form, classify urgency, route to the right queue/staff, and book the slot — the receptionist approves with one tap. Bengali + English voice-first.
demo: Three walk-ins speak over each other; three clean case cards appear, one flagged urgent and auto-bumped — the queue never stopped moving.

title: Permit Path
pitch: A site photo plus your business type returns the full permit checklist — who to see, in what order, with what papers
problem: Opening a shop means 6 offices, 11 forms and folklore advice. People burn weeks and bribes on steps they didn't know existed; the sequence is different for every business type.
how: Photograph the premises, answer 5 questions; Spark (search-grounded with citations) builds the personalized permit path: authority, document, fee, sequence — printable checklist with QR links to portals.
demo: Pick 'cold-storage restaurant': the 9-step path prints with the two parallel branches highlighted — the answer that took the presenter 3 weeks takes 20 seconds.

title: Vendor Drift Radar
pitch: Incoming-goods photos are checked against the agreed spec; vendor drift gets receipts, not vibes
problem: Suppliers quietly degrade quality: thinner fabric, fewer units per bundle, wrong finish. Rejections are argued case-by-case because nobody kept comparative evidence.
how: Goods-in photos are segmented and measured (count, dimension via reference card, finish class); Spark compares against the spec and the vendor's own history; a drift chart builds per vendor with evidence packs for negotiation.
demo: Two delivery photos a month apart: the radar shows stitch density drift with both photos side-by-side — the negotiation ends before it starts.

title: Night Shift Oracle
pitch: Glimmer on the shop's old laptop: the expert that stays all night, answering from the plant's own manuals
problem: At 3am there is no expert — just a junior with a flashlight and a 400-page manual. Calls to sleeping seniors cost response time; small errors compound into shutdowns.
how: Muse Glimmer (Apache 2.0) self-hosts on the site's old laptop with the plant's manuals indexed; night crew asks by voice in their language; Spark pre-builds the procedure cards offline; internet only logs the incident after.
demo: Flip the Wi-Fi off: ask 'chiller 2 pressure dropping, what first?' — the offline oracle answers from the plant's own manual, in Bengali, in seconds.
